calls.head: The Blues like Suter’s line against Poitras’s
calls.body: At home, the Blues keep sending Suter’s line (Kaskimäki, Suter and Stenberg) out against opponents’ fourth lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Jim Montgomery keeps choosing line for line. Tonight the Bruins’ fourth line is Jeannot, Kastelic and Poitras.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Thomas has a goal and two assists as the Blues take down the Bruins
paras: James Hagens got the scoring started for the Bruins early in the first, but they didn’t score again. Jimmy Snuggerud tied it up for St. Louis on the power play late in the period, and Philip Broberg gave the Blues the lead early in the second. Robert Thomas made it 3-1 midway through the period. Jake Neighbours stretched the lead to 4-1 on the power play with a little over seven minutes left. Thomas and Broberg each had a goal and two assists.

The Bruins outshot the Blues 32-18, but the Blues’ looks were better, so the chances came out about even. The Bruins hit two posts and the crossbar, and the bounces never came. Joel Hofer made 31 saves for the Blues, and Jeremy Swayman stopped 14 of 18 at the other end. The Blues improved to 6-6-1 and climbed to fifth in the Central, while the Bruins fell to 9-4-1, still first in the Atlantic.

items.text: Robert Thomas passed Brian Sutter for fourth on the Blues’ all-time assists list, with 335.
The Bruins’ Connor Clifton was back in the lineup after missing seven games.
The Blues bounced back after two straight losses.
Jonatan Berggren faces his old team, Detroit, on Saturday.
